rejudgement.rules: every trial judged again from what it stored: the verdict through `judge_trial` (engine-side failures -- failed, refused and partially rejected requests, the durable buffer's growing log, ingest failures and rejected bundles -- outrank producer lateness), the generator read-back's aggregate equalities (stored rows less stored failed-request rows equal the acknowledged records, every stored record once, the sequence sum when no failed request's rows were stored), and the Alloy read-back through `judge_read_back` (a duplicate fails it)

rules.admission_ceiling: strict records/s per worker <= receiver slots x records per request / hold time, a window plus the flush that makes a block durable
rules.raised_search_seed: the raised search starts from the shipped search's bracket: its sustainable rate is taken as sustainable and its first trial is the shipped unsustainable rate
rules.rss_band: the anonymous RSS growth since the first allocator print lies between the growth of jemalloc `allocated` (lower edge) and the growth of the most jemalloc held resident over the interval the kernel may still be releasing: the maximum of `resident` at this print, at any print read with it, and at the previous paired print (upper edge); a residual beyond max(32 MiB, 0.10 x peak RSS) fails. After a large purge jemalloc stops counting an extent as resident before the kernel has released its pages, so an RSS read milliseconds after the print can still hold them (soak-strict r002: five reads 122-234 MB above resident, inside the band at the next print 11-49 ms later)
rules.search_floor_rule: a cell after the first may start at half of min(the one-worker ceiling on the same store times the workers, the shipped-slot formula ceiling), rounded down to the doubling grid; an unsustainable first trial halves until one passes
rules.search_interval_override: one-second windows instead of the shipped 15 s, so a bounded producer concurrency does not cap the strict hold time

alloy-file.description: Grafana Alloy tailing one file of 100-byte lines through the reference River config, batches of 20000 to 50000 records

logs-1k-hot.description: logs only, 1KiB bodies, 10k series slots cycled per record

metrics-1k-hot.description: metric points only, 10k series slots cycled per point

metrics-1k-unique.description: metric points only, one attribute unique per point, so every point is a new series

mixed-1k-churn.description: every request brings new series: one logs series and one slot per request, never repeated

mixed-1k-hot.description: 80/20 logs/metric points by record, 1KiB bodies, 10k series slots cycled per record

mixed-8k-hot.description: the 8KiB-body variant of mixed-1k-hot; its 8 MB log requests exceed the receiver's default 4 MiB decoding limit, so it runs with 16 MiB

stage_join.reason: no attribution family ran this workload, configuration and core allocation; Task 4 shares are for logs-1k-stable and metrics-mixed at 100 records per request with 128-request blocks
